candidates.title: Full AttnRes with Canon layers (baseline reproduction)
candidates.hypothesis: Session anchor: reproduction of the published attnres_full_canon_abcd (Full Attention Residuals + Canon-A/B/C/D) as a plugin, to measure the research trainer's dev BPB and training-loss curve for the best published method.

candidates.title: Hashed n-gram memory + Full AttnRes + Canon-A/B/C/D
candidates.hypothesis: Hashed n-gram memory (zero-FLOP lookups of signed, multi-hash bigram/trigram embeddings, trained by auxiliary AdamW) added to depth source b0 of Full AttnRes + Canon-A/B/C/D. Closest prior: attnres_full_canon_abcd (trunk), DeepSeek Engram and the modded-nanogpt/nanochat bigram hash embedding (memory). Difference: the memory enters the embedding source that every sublayer and the readout read through depth attention, uses several signed hash heads per order and a low-dimensional table with one projection.

candidates.title: Hashed n-gram memory + Full AttnRes + Canon-A/B/C/D
candidates.hypothesis: Full Attention Residuals + Canon-A/B/C/D (the published attnres_full_canon_abcd trunk) extended along two axes. (1) A hashed bigram embedding memory: zero-initialized embedding tables indexed by multiplicative hashes of the (previous, current) token pair, written into depth source b0 (the token embedding) so that every sublayer and the readout reach it through AttnRes depth attention, optionally also added to the gated value embeddings; lookups add parameters but no matrix FLOPs. (2) Depth-read refinements that all start as the identity: a channel-grouped depth softmax, a static per-source logit bias, separate depth reads for the query, key and value inputs of each attention sublayer, and Canon layers on block outputs, on the gated value embeddings and on the final read. Closest prior methods: attnres_full_canon_abcd (Kimi Attention Residuals + Allen-Zhu Canon layers), MSAR (multi-stream depth reads with temporal taps on writes), DenseFormer (static depth weights), the bigram hash embedding of modded-nanogpt PR #201 / nanochat Engram-lite, DeepSeek Engram and MoME (lookup memories). Differences: the memory enters through the embedding depth source instead of per-layer residual scalars or context gates; depth attention is per channel group and per attention input (q/k/v) instead of one read per sublayer; Canon also acts on writes, value embeddings and the readout. The options in architecture.json state which refinements are active.

candidates.title: Hashed n-gram memory + Full AttnRes + Canon-A/B/C/D
candidates.hypothesis: Full Attention Residuals + Canon-A/B/C/D (the published attnres_full_canon_abcd trunk) with two additions. (1) Canon wherever a token-level signal is written or read: besides the Canon layers on sublayer inputs (A/C), on q/k/v (B) and on the MLP hidden (D), a zero-initialized causal depthwise convolution also filters every completed block output before it becomes a depth source, the embedding source b0, the gated value embeddings (Canon-B on v acts after the value embedding is added) and the final depth read; kernels are widened from 4 to 8 (sublayer inputs, q/k/v, MLP hidden, readout) and 12 (depth-source writes). (2) A hashed bigram embedding memory: 2 signed multiplicative-hash lookups of the (previous, current) token pair into zero-initialized embedding tables (320,000 rows x 768 each), concatenated to the model width, scaled by 0.1 and added to the token embedding, i.e. to depth source b0, which every sublayer and the readout reach through depth attention; the tables add about 0.49B parameters and no matrix FLOPs and train in the shell's embedding AdamW group. Closest prior methods: attnres_full_canon_abcd (Kimi Attention Residuals + Allen-Zhu's Canon layers); MSAR (causal convolution taps with kernels 4/8/12 on depth sources, kept as separate streams); the bigram hash embedding of modded-nanogpt PR #201 / nanochat Engram-lite and DeepSeek Engram (hashed n-gram memories). Differences: unlike attnres_full_canon_abcd, Canon also filters the depth sources themselves (block outputs and embedding), the value embeddings and the readout, with wider kernels; unlike MSAR, each source gets one learned filter added in place (no extra streams, queries or gates) inside a Full AttnRes + Canon-ABCD trunk; unlike Engram and Engram-lite, the memory is written once into the embedding depth source and is read by every sublayer and by the readout through AttnRes depth attention instead of per-layer residual scalars or context gates, and it uses signed hash heads. The other plugin options (grouped depth reads, depth bias, separate q/k/v depth reads, value-path memory) were tried in research and are switched off. Research evidence (session runs of 1,024 updates under the frozen schedule, same data order, against a plugin reproduction of attnres_full_canon_abcd): dev BPB 0.8336 against 0.8416, and training loss lower by 0.028 nats per token over updates 897-1,024; the bigram memory alone accounts for about half of that early gap and its share shrinks with training, while the added Canon layers give a steadier gain.
